title: Teleop episode QA: frames, sync and validity
scenario: Measure each teleoperation episode (distinct camera frames, duration, frame gaps, camera-to-joint sync), apply validity rules per robot, and summarise valid episodes per task. Test 3 reports usable minutes.

verified.why_correct: The slice `sorted_ts[max(i - 1, 0):i + 1]` looks like it could miss a neighbour or go out of range, but bisect_left puts t between index i-1 and i, so those are the only two candidates, the slice clamps at both ends, and an empty list returns None.

bugs.title: Repeated camera timestamps counted as frames
bugs.symptom: test_1_frame_counts fails: EP01 shows 32 frames instead of 30 and EP07 32 instead of 31. Gaps, durations and sync rates are unchanged.
bugs.why: The camera log repeats some timestamps, and the spec counts one frame per distinct timestamp. Sorting without set() keeps the repeats. They add 0 ms gaps and are always matched, so only the frame count changes.
hints: Only EP01 and EP07 have too many frames. Look at their camera_ms lists in frames.json.
Look at how the raw camera timestamps become frames.
probes: Why didn't the extra frames change max_gap_ms or duration_s?
Under what data would the repeats have changed sync_rate as well?

bugs.title: Duration floored to whole seconds
bugs.symptom: test_2_durations fails: every duration is a whole number (EP01 2 instead of 2.9, EP03 2 instead of 2.44, EP08 3 instead of 3.06, EP09 3 instead of 3.9 ...). Validity is unchanged.
bugs.why: `//` floors the millisecond span to whole seconds before round() runs, so 2.9 s becomes 2. It never changes the too_short check, because floor(x) >= 2 exactly when x >= 2.
hints: Every duration is a whole number. Is that plausible?
Look at how span_ms is turned into seconds.
probes: Why didn't the validity tests notice whole-second durations?
If min_duration_s were 2.5, what would this have done to EP01?

bugs.title: Sync tolerance made exclusive
bugs.old: if gap is not None and gap <= tolerance_ms:
bugs.new: if gap is not None and gap < tolerance_ms:
bugs.symptom: test_3_sync_rates fails: EP02 drops to 0.951 and EP10 to 0.941 instead of 1.0. Neither falls below 0.9, so validity is unchanged.
bugs.why: The spec says a joint sample exactly sync_tolerance_ms away still counts. With `<`, frames exactly 10 ms from their nearest joint sample stop matching.
hints: EP02 and EP10 lose a few matches. How far are their unmatched frames from the nearest joint sample?
Check the tolerance comparison in sync_rate against metrics rule 5.
probes: Why didn't EP02 or EP10 become unsynced?
How would you test the boundary so this fails loudly?

bugs.title: "no"/"false" robots treated as active
bugs.symptom: test_4_inactive_robots fails: no episode is flagged robot_inactive ([] instead of ['EP05', 'EP09']). The valid set is unchanged because both episodes break other rules.
bugs.why: bool() of a non-empty string is always True, so RB-04 (`no`) and RB-07 (`false`) load as active and their episodes lose the robot_inactive reason. Both episodes are invalid for other reasons too, so the valid set doesn't change.
hints: No episode is flagged robot_inactive. Which robots are inactive in robots.csv?
Look at how the `active` column is parsed.
parse_bool should return text.lower() in TRUTHY.
probes: Why does a blank `active` cell still come out active with the original code?

bugs.title: Gap equal to the limit flagged
bugs.old: if robot is not None and metrics.max_gap_ms > robot.max_gap_ms:
bugs.new: if robot is not None and metrics.max_gap_ms >= robot.max_gap_ms:
bugs.symptom: test_5_frame_gaps fails: frame_gap is ['EP06', 'EP08'] instead of ['EP08']. EP06 is already unsynced, so the valid set is unchanged.
bugs.why: The spec flags a gap only when it is greater than the robot's limit. `>=` also flags EP06, whose largest gap is exactly 150 ms on a robot whose limit is 150 ms.
hints: EP06 is flagged frame_gap. Compare its max_gap_ms with its robot's limit.
Look at the frame_gap rule in validity.py.
probes: Why didn't EP03 (140 ms gap) get flagged?
Why is EP06 invalid either way?

bugs.title: Valid time divided as if it were seconds
bugs.symptom: test_6_valid_minutes fails: valid_minutes is 366.83 instead of 0.37.
bugs.why: The spans are in milliseconds. Dividing by 60 treats them as seconds, so the total is 1000 times too large.
hints: Seven episodes of 2–5 seconds can't add up to 366 minutes.
Check the units of span_ms in the valid_minutes calculation.
probes: Why does the spec say to use the raw spans and not the rounded duration_s values?
How would you name variables so that a unit slip like this is harder to make?

context_qa.q: What is the flow inside build_report()?
context_qa.a: It loads the thresholds, the robots and the episodes (metadata from episodes.csv, timestamps from frames.json). For each episode it calls `metrics.compute_metrics`, then `validity.check_episode` with that episode's robot, and collects rows of episode, metrics and reasons. The episodes table is built from those rows and `summarize(rows)` builds the summary.

context_qa.q: How does load_episodes match frames.json entries to CSV rows?
context_qa.a: It builds a dict keyed by the upper-cased, trimmed `episode_id` from frames.json, then looks each normalised CSV episode id up in it. An id missing from frames.json gets empty timestamp lists, and frames.json entries without a CSV row are never read.
The absolute distance in ms from `t` to the closest value in the sorted list, using bisect to look only at the neighbours on either side, or None if the list is empty.

context_qa.q: What fields does EpisodeMetrics carry, and in what units?
context_qa.a: `frames` (count), `span_ms` (last minus first frame, ms), `duration_s` (seconds, from span_ms), `max_gap_ms` (ms) and `sync_rate` (a fraction from 0 to 1).

context_qa.q: What decides whether an episode counts as valid in the summary?
context_qa.a: A row is valid when its `reasons` list is empty. `summarize` groups rows by task and computes valid counts and success rates from those rows, and `valid_minutes` sums `span_ms` over valid rows.

context_qa.q: Where does a robot's max_gap_ms come from?
context_qa.a: From robots.csv, parsed to int in `load_robots`. `check_episode` compares the episode's `max_gap_ms` against it whenever the robot is known.

context_qa.q: How is success parsed for an episode?
context_qa.a: In `load_episodes`: the cell is trimmed, lower-cased and checked for membership in `TRUTHY` (`true`, `yes`, `y`, `1`).
